Let me read the part index and then start checking wilt-related candidates.
Whole plant is the relevant part. Top wilt candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt. Let me check reference images one at a time.
Bacterial_Wilt shows severe brown/dead drooping plants on staked setup. The test image plants are wilted but more green, in an open field without stakes. Let me check Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt shows a single plant wilting acutely on plastic mulch. Test image is open field rows with widespread but partial plant collapse. Let me check Verticillium_Wilt.

Verticillium_Wilt reference is a leaf close-up with V-shaped lesions — not matching the whole-plant field view. Let me check Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus (causes stunting/bushy plants) and Late_Blight for comparison.

This reference image is an exact match to the test image — same field, same Bugwood ID 1568048. This is **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus**. The plants show the characteristic stunted, bushy appearance with lighter-colored foliage visible from a field-level perspective, consistent with CMV causing stunting and mosaic.

I still need to view 4 more reference images (budget requires 8 total across at least 8 different classes). Let me check the remaining classes quickly.

The Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus reference `Bugwood_18.jpg` (Bugwood ID 1568048) is a pixel-perfect match to the test image — same field, same rows, same perspective.
